subject: ICE Actions and Constitutional Rights
overview: The Council approved a resolution condemning a recent ICE killing in Minneapolis and referred related local policy reviews to committee. Additionally, the Council approved capital funding for a school repair study and passed a first reading of an ordinance banning face surveillance technology.

items.title: Clarence Ed Ligon Condolences
items.summary: Approved a resolution sending deep condolences to the family of West Medford community pillar Clarence "Ed" Ligon, Jr.

items.title: Meeting Minutes and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the January 6, 2026 meeting and the Committee of the Whole report regarding EMS changes and the city clerk hiring process.

items.title: Common Victualler's License for Annie's Pizzeria
items.summary: Approved a common victualler's license for KNC Made LLC, doing business as Annie's Pizzeria, at 213 Middlesex Avenue.

items.title: Litigation Executive Session
items.summary: Voted to enter executive session to discuss strategy regarding De Silva v. City of Medford litigation.

items.title: Roberts Elementary School Feasibility Study Funding
items.summary: Approved a $300,000 appropriation from the Capital Stabilization Fund for an MSBA feasibility study on a roof and heat pump project at Roberts Elementary School, and scheduled a future committee meeting to review all ongoing school building projects.

items.title: Resolution on ICE Actions and Constitutional Rights
items.summary: Approved a resolution condemning the killing of Renee Nicole Goode by ICE in Minneapolis and reaffirming residents' right to document law enforcement, while referring proposed local policing strategies and school protections to the Committee on Public Health and Community Safety.

items.title: Employee Vacation Ordinance Amendment
items.summary: Referred a proposed ordinance change to increase vacation time for city employees in their first five years of service to the Administration and Finance Committee.

items.title: Face Surveillance Technology Ban Ordinance
items.summary: Passed on first reading a proposed ordinance banning municipal acquisition, possession, or use of face surveillance systems.
